errors.description: The model hallucinated that each cube has only one color (i.e., is monochromatic), which is not supported by the Scene Description or Ground Truth. In reality, each cube has six different colored faces, as explicitly detailed in the Ground Truth Reasoning. The model incorrectly assumed that the color shown on the front face is the cube’s only color, leading to a fundamentally flawed mental model of the scene.

errors.evidence_quote: The hidden faces are the other five faces, which include all colors except the one visible on the front.
errors.description: The model incorrectly assumed that hidden faces of a cube contain all colors except the front-facing one. This is a structural hallucination — cubes do not contain every color on their hidden faces; each face has a fixed, pre-assigned color. The model invented a rule that doesn’t exist in the scene, leading to a mathematically uniform but factually incorrect distribution of hidden colors.

errors.description: The model built its entire reasoning on the false premise that each cube is monochromatic and that hidden faces contain all other colors. Even though it correctly deduced that all colors would be equally frequent under this false assumption, the premise itself is invalid. The model then attempted to justify choosing 'yellow' as the answer based on sequence position — a heuristic not grounded in the actual scene data.
